cases.reason: Format (GROUP-USAGE IS BIT|NATIONAL) identical. The words differ: 2002 'A USAGE clause shall not be specified', 2023 'shall not be explicitly specified ... but USAGE BIT may be implicitly specified'. In 2002 a group-level USAGE applies only to elementary items (USAGE GR1), so the subject never has an implicit USAGE clause and the two sentences forbid the same program (probe ws_gu_implicit.cob: an enclosing USAGE BIT group over a GROUP-USAGE BIT subgroup is accepted at 2002 and 2023). The difference is evidence and reach: in 2002 the rule also governs a record under a CD, and two of the twin's legs have no witness at 2002 (the BIT explicit-USAGE and non-boolean-subordinate legs; the positive witness does not translate at 2002). Every probe shows the compiler correct.
